discipline: Biostatistics / Quality Improvement / Health Services Research
diagnosis: Interrupted time-series analysis using segmented regression
mechanism: Interrupted time-series designs use repeated outcome measurements before and after an intervention. Segmented regression estimates the preintervention trend and tests whether the intervention is associated with an immediate level change, a change in postintervention slope, or both, helping distinguish an intervention effect from the preexisting secular trend.
vignette: A hospital introduces a new sepsis triage protocol on January 1. Investigators have monthly median time-to-antibiotics data for 24 months before implementation and 24 months after implementation. The outcome had already been gradually improving before the protocol was introduced. Randomization was not feasible.
lead: Which of the following analytic approaches is most appropriate for estimating whether the protocol changed the outcome beyond the preexisting trend?
correct: Segmented regression of an interrupted time series estimating changes in level and slope after implementation
distractors: Compare the mean outcome during all preintervention months with the mean during all postintervention months using an unpaired t test
Perform a cross-sectional correlation between calendar month and the outcome using only postintervention observations
Select the single month before implementation and the single month after implementation and calculate their absolute difference
Pool all observations and use a chi-square test without including time or intervention terms
distractor_notes: A simple before-versus-after comparison ignores the existing time trend and temporal structure.
Postintervention data alone cannot estimate the counterfactual trajectory based on the preintervention trend.
Two adjacent points are highly vulnerable to ordinary temporal variation and discard most available information.
Ignoring time and intervention structure cannot estimate level or slope changes attributable to implementation.
key_expl: Interrupted time-series analysis is useful when an intervention occurs at a defined time and repeated measurements are available before and after it. Segmented regression models the baseline level and trend and estimates an immediate level change and/or a change in slope after the intervention. This directly addresses the concern that the outcome was already improving before implementation.
objective: Choose segmented interrupted time-series regression to evaluate a quality-improvement intervention when repeated pre/post measurements and a preexisting secular trend are present.
